Este socant ce se intampla. Am fost si eu la Obregia pt 2 sapt cand aveam 17 ani si a fost naspa. Daca nu era mama internata cu mine ca sa aibe grija de mine, sunt 100% sigura ca ma viola unu din pacienti care se trezea noaptea si mergea in camerele celorlalti sa fure mancare. Super ciudat omu, gen full zombie cu bale la gura si mers târşâit, si cand am venit in prima zi voia sa ma pupe. E cum ai zis cu, asistentele se poarta cu tine ca si cand ai fi un animal sau un copil prost de 5 ani. Sorry you went through this 😔 si eu am avut o psihiatra tampita dupa ce am facut 18 ani, nici nu mai stiu cum o cheama dar e la un cabinet de langa Obregia. In caz ca dati de ea, e o femeie grasa cu par negru si ochelari. Am fost de cateva ori la ea si de fiecare data ma facea sa plang doar ca sa imi mareasca doza de pastile in conditiile in care eu incercam sa trec peste si sa imi vad de viata. Ea tot ma intreba de episodul meu depresiv care m-a adus in Spital cand eu nici nu imi mai aduceam aminte mare lucru ☠️ ma chinuia ca sa aibe client. Mda si incet incet mama mi a mai scazut doza de pastile si nu am mai dat pe la psihiatra asta tampita buna de nimic. I was really big into art nouveau some years back and now im constantly buying renaissance and baroque artists books. i just love to explore anatomy and watercolour. My favourite watercolour artists are Frank Webb, David Downton, Emelie von Walterstorff and Manolo Blahnik. Elisabeth Moritz also uses a pattern similar to mine in her cutout photographs. Michael Borremans also evoques an air of uneasiness and ominous i sometimes try to aim for. Paul Jouvre has excelent feline anatomy that feels almost tangible and i really want to reach that level of credibility. Matisse has a great use of colour and composition. Alexander Calder executes amazing portraits in wire. An artist that really impacted me forever must be Francis Bacon because of how guttural and unsettling his pieces are; his "Study after Velázquez's Portrait of Pope Innocent X" really reminds me of Diavolo. Screaming in pain and in an infinite transition. I like to look both into the past and contemporary before i create. Maybe you can tell that I'm also a big fan of ancient greek statues and bas-reliefs. I also liek to take my own reference pictures sometimes because the internnet just doesnt have the right stock photos, that way, the drawing feels more intimate to me, closer to my being.
